dedupe_keys.name: bostontwin ray tracing ready 3d model of boston with cellular base station locations

description: BostonTwin is a dataset that merges a high-fidelity 3D model of the city of Boston, Massachusetts, with existing geospatial data on cellular base station deployments, in a ray-tracing-ready format. The paper argues that digital twins are a staple of wireless network design and that 6G, with extended reality and immersive communications, will rely on them; BostonTwin gives instantaneous rendering and programmatic access to the building models and an accurate representation of the electromagnetic propagation environment. Producer: Testolina, Polese, Johari and Melodia (Northeastern University wireless research group), presented at the ACM Multimedia Systems Conference 2024 in Bari, Italy (7 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables), submitted to arXiv on 18 March 2024. Coverage: the city of Boston. Access: the abstract page describes the dataset and links the paper; where the files can be downloaded was not confirmed on the page read. Licence and cost: not stated for the dataset; the paper is free (arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence). Caveats: the model represents buildings and base station positions at one time, and results depend on the ray tracer chosen. Simulation uses: it is an input for wireless digital twins, coverage prediction and capacity planning in dense urban areas. Related record: the Open Wireless Digital Twin (platform-open-wireless-digital-twin-oai-sionna), which also combines ray tracing with building data.
